text:
Brett Howden plays the kind of minutes that rarely show up on a scoresheet, and this season the scoresheet has been especially unkind. He has 8 goals and 12 points in 26 games, none on the power play, while Vegas has scored 9.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. That usually swings back.

His own game has grown. He's generating 1.11 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, up from 0.62 last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of plenty of passes across the slot or from behind the net. He's quick, too: 92nd percentile for bursts over 20 mph. Jake Oettinger robbed him on a backdoor two-on-one with Jack Eichel on Nov. 19, the kind of chance that, as Jesse Granger described it, took an "incredible read" to stop.

The concern is five-on-five control. Vegas gets only 50% of the expected goals with him on, worse than without him. He scored and added an assist in the shootout win at Winnipeg.

A 2023 Cup winner doing third-line work, with points owed to him.
headline: Howden is better than his points
